chunks: It is as though you too have gone where they have gone,
the same sleeping place has caught you and the same place has detained you.
What will then be your position when your affairs reach their end and graves are turned upside down (to throw out the dead)?
“There shall every soul realise what it hath sent before, and they shall be brought back to Allāh, their true Lord, and what they did fabricate (the false deities) will vanish (away) from them.”
ai.seo_question: What does Nahj al-Balagha say about the reality of death and the grave?
ai.summary: Imam Ali employs the rhetorical device of *isti'dhar* (imagery of the grave) to transition from the physical reality of burial to the spiritual accountability of the Hereafter, a hallmark of his eloquent style in *Nahj al-Balagha*. This passage underscores the Shia concept of *Barzakh* as a transitional realm where the soul prepares for the ultimate trial (*Balwa*) of individual deeds, reinforcing the inevitability of returning to Allah as the true Sovereign.
